cobra.definition: Venomous Asiatic and African elapid snakes that can expand the skin of the neck into a hood.
cobra.exampleUsage: The cobra expanded the skin around its neck into a hood.

python.definition: A large snake that kills prey by squeezing it.
python.exampleUsage: The python rested in loops beneath the enclosure shelter.

rattlesnake.definition: Pit viper with horny segments at the end of the tail that rattle when shaken.
rattlesnake.exampleUsage: The rattlesnake shook the segments at the end of its tail.

boa.definition: A large snake that wraps around prey and squeezes it.
boa.exampleUsage: The boa rested on a branch in the managed enclosure.

viper.definition: A snake of the viper family, typically with long hinged venom-delivering fangs.
viper.exampleUsage: The viper in the reference has hinged venom-delivering fangs.

corn-snake.definition: A nonvenomous North American snake with orange, reddish, or brown blotched coloring, commonly kept in zoological collections and as a pet.
corn-snake.exampleUsage: The corn snake rested beneath a shelter in the exhibit.

king-snake.definition: A nonvenomous snake of the genus Lampropeltis, known for eating a varied diet that can include other snakes.
king-snake.exampleUsage: The king snake moved slowly across its enclosure.

anaconda.definition: A large South American boa adapted strongly to life in or near water.
anaconda.exampleUsage: The anaconda swam through the managed water area.

mamba.definition: A venomous African snake of the mamba group.
mamba.exampleUsage: The verified reference identifies the mamba as an African snake.

garter-snake.definition: A generally small, slender North American snake of the genus Thamnophis, often marked with lengthwise stripes.
garter-snake.exampleUsage: A garter snake was visible near the water feature.

gecko.definition: A lizard of the gecko group; activity patterns, eyelids and other features vary by species.
gecko.exampleUsage: The gecko rested on the enclosure wall.

iguana.definition: Large herbivorous tropical American arboreal lizards with a spiny crest along the back.
iguana.exampleUsage: The iguana's spiny crest was visible along its back.

chameleon.definition: Lizard of Africa and Madagascar able to change skin color and having a projectile tongue.
chameleon.exampleUsage: The chameleon gripped the branch with its feet.

monitor.definition: A lizard of the monitor group, often with a long neck, strong limbs, and long tail.
monitor.exampleUsage: The monitor lizard walked across the enclosure ground.

skink.definition: Alert agile lizard with reduced limbs and an elongated body covered with shiny scales.
skink.exampleUsage: The skink moved quickly beneath the shelter.

bearded-dragon.definition: An Australian lizard with spiny scales around the throat that can form a beard-like display.
bearded-dragon.exampleUsage: The bearded dragon rested under the managed enclosure light.

anole.definition: Small arboreal tropical American insectivorous lizards with the ability to change skin color.
anole.exampleUsage: The anole perched on a branch above the plants.

komodo-dragon.definition: The world's largest living lizard, native to several Indonesian islands.
komodo-dragon.exampleUsage: The Komodo dragon walked across the protected habitat.

basilisk.definition: A tropical American lizard; some species can run briefly across water.
basilisk.exampleUsage: The observed basilisk ran briefly across the water surface.

horned-lizard.definition: A broad-bodied lizard, mainly from North and Central America, with pointed scales or horns around the head.
horned-lizard.exampleUsage: The horned lizard blended with the sandy ground.

turtle.definition: A reptile with a shell enclosing much of its body; the broad name includes aquatic and land-adapted groups.
turtle.exampleUsage: The turtle withdrew its head beneath its shell.

tortoise.definition: Usually herbivorous land turtles having clawed elephant-like limbs.
tortoise.exampleUsage: The tortoise walked across the dry enclosure floor.

sea-turtle.definition: Large turtles that spend most of their lives in tropical or subtropical oceans come ashore mainly to lay eggs on sandy beaches.
sea-turtle.exampleUsage: The sea turtle returned to the ocean after nesting.

snapping-turtle.definition: A large freshwater turtle with powerful jaws and a long tail, known for defensive snapping when threatened.
snapping-turtle.exampleUsage: Visitors observed the snapping turtle from outside the enclosure.

crocodile.definition: Large voracious aquatic reptile having a long snout with massive jaws and sharp teeth and a body covered with bony plates.
crocodile.exampleUsage: The crocodile rested beside the managed water area.

alligator.definition: A large reptile related to crocodiles, with a broad snout.
alligator.exampleUsage: The alligator moved through the shallow water.

caiman.definition: A semiaquatic reptile of Central and South America that resembles an alligator but has a more heavily armored belly.
caiman.exampleUsage: The caiman remained partly submerged near the bank.

terrapin.definition: A turtle associated with fresh or brackish water; the common-name usage varies by region.
terrapin.exampleUsage: The terrapin rested beside the water in the exhibit.

softshell.definition: A freshwater turtle with a flattened body and a flexible leathery shell rather than a hard scaly shell.
softshell.exampleUsage: The softshell turtle rested on the sandy bottom.

gharial.definition: A long-snouted crocodilian native to rivers of the Indian subcontinent and adapted mainly for catching fish.
gharial.exampleUsage: The gharial swam with its long narrow snout above the water.

scale.definition: A small plate-like structure forming part of a reptile’s outer skin.
scale.exampleUsage: The close-up reference shows a scale from the reptile's skin.

shell.definition: The protective body structure enclosing much of a turtle’s body.
shell.exampleUsage: The turtle's shell covers much of its body.

fang.definition: A long pointed tooth, sometimes used to inject venom.
fang.exampleUsage: The anatomical reference identifies the snake's specialized fang.

tongue.definition: A muscular mouth organ used in feeding and sensory functions, with roles varying by species.
tongue.exampleUsage: The snake extended its tongue while exploring its surroundings.

tail.definition: The part extending from the rear of an animal's body.
tail.exampleUsage: The lizard's tail extended behind its body.

claw.definition: Sharp curved horny process on the toe of a bird or some mammals or reptiles.
claw.exampleUsage: The lizard gripped the surface with a claw.

eye.definition: The sensory organ used for vision.
eye.exampleUsage: The lizard turned its eye toward the movement.

jaw.definition: The part of the skull of a vertebrate that frames the mouth and holds the teeth.
jaw.exampleUsage: The jaw supports the reptile's teeth and mouth opening.

skin.definition: A natural protective body covering and site of the sense of touch.
skin.exampleUsage: The reptile's skin forms its outer body covering.

venom.exampleUsage: The scientific account describes venom delivered through a specialized bite.
venom.definition: A toxic secretion introduced through a bite, sting, or other specialized delivery structure.

terrarium.definition: An enclosure designed for keeping suitable terrestrial animals or plants under controlled conditions.
terrarium.exampleUsage: Staff manage conditions inside the terrarium for its resident species.

heat-lamp.definition: A lamp selected to supply heat under an enclosure’s managed requirements.
heat-lamp.exampleUsage: The heat lamp supplies warmth under the enclosure's managed requirements.

water-dish.definition: A shallow container kept filled with water so animals can drink from it.
water-dish.exampleUsage: The lizard drank from the shallow water dish.

branch.definition: A woody part that grows from a tree trunk or large branch.
branch.exampleUsage: The lizard climbed onto the branch.

rock.definition: A hard natural material found on the ground.
rock.exampleUsage: The lizard rested beside the rock in its enclosure.

sand.definition: Small loose grains of rock or mineral material.
sand.exampleUsage: Loose sand covered part of the managed enclosure floor.

moss.exampleUsage: Moss grew in the damp part of the managed habitat.

hide.definition: A sheltered place where a captive reptile can stay out of view.
hide.exampleUsage: The reptile rested out of view inside the hide.

log.definition: A piece of a tree trunk used in a reptile enclosure.
log.exampleUsage: The lizard climbed over the fallen log.

misting-system.definition: An engineered setup that sprays tiny water droplets to control heat, moisture, or airborne particles in enclosed settings.
misting-system.exampleUsage: Staff controlled moisture through the enclosure's misting system.

shed.definition: To lose the old outer skin covering during growth or renewal.
shed.exampleUsage: Snakes shed their old outer skin during growth and renewal.

bask.definition: To rest in warmth, often in sunlight.
bask.exampleUsage: Some reptiles bask in warmth to help regulate body temperature.

hunt.definition: To search for and catch animals for food.
hunt.exampleUsage: Predatory reptiles hunt for suitable prey.

swim.definition: To move through water using the arms, legs, or body.
swim.exampleUsage: Aquatic reptiles swim through the managed water area.

burrow.definition: To move through by or as by digging.
burrow.exampleUsage: Some reptiles burrow into suitable ground material.

climb.definition: To move upward using feet, claws, or the body.
climb.exampleUsage: The lizards climb the branches in their enclosure.

camouflage.definition: Appearance or behavior that makes an animal less noticeable against its surroundings.
camouflage.exampleUsage: The reptile's camouflage made it less noticeable against the ground.

hiss.definition: To produce a sibilant blowing sound.

strike.definition: To attack suddenly, as a snake does when biting.
strike.exampleUsage: A snake can strike with a rapid attacking movement.

coil.definition: To curl the body into loops.
coil.exampleUsage: The snakes coil their bodies into loops.
